html:
Paneer (cottage cheese) is  a milk based ingredient, and can be used to prepare a number of dishes. Like Paneer butter masala,  paneer pakodas (cottage cheese fritters),these dishes are yum but can be quite heavy so some times one  feels like just having the paneer (cottage cheese) prepared in a lighter and quicker way, this is just that dish and kids love it too:) great for Vegetarians!!


Ingredients:
500 gm paneer (cottage cheese) cut into cubes
1 medium green bell pepper cut into little cubes
1 small onion cubed small
1 inch ginger piece chopped fine
2 to 3 cloves of garlic crushed
2 green chilies chopped fine
1 tsp salt ( as per taste)
1/2 tsp red chili powder
1/2 tsp cumin seeds
1 tsp coriander seeds
1 tsp kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves)
1/3 cup water.


Paneer Kadai Subzi



Method:
1.Heat oil. in a wok. Add cumin seeds, coriander seeds,allow to splutter.Add in diced onions, stir and   brown a little add in tomatoes,continue cooking on low heat.
2.Add the bell pepper,ginger ,garlic ,salt,red chili powder.Add 1/3 cup water and cover with a lid for about 5 minutes to allow capsicum to get softened but not too soft.Add the paneer cubes, stirring gently, simmer for another 3 to 4 minutes and your kadai paneer is ready.
3.Garnish with dried fenugreek leaves or freshly chopped coriander leaves. Serve hot with Indian bread.
Just takes less than  20 minutes to serve an easy to prepare healthy dish for you and your family.

Ingredients:

Crunchy Karele





Method:

2.Heat 4 tsp  oil in a wok, add cumin seeds, allow them to crackle, add the sliced onions,allow them to turn slightly golden brown , then add in karela, stir and cover to cook  them on low heat  for 10 to 12 minutes. As they soften add in cashews and raisins..
3.Continue cooking on medium heat till the karela appear lightly browned and crisp.Add 1 tsp jaggery and coriander powder,stir for 5 minutes and close burner.Serve them along with Indian bread as aside dish.

html:
Friends, today I would like to share the recipe of a famous North Indian dish, Dal Makhani. It is popularly also known as Kaali Dal or Maa Ki Dal. 


The secret to a good tasty Dal makhani, is to soak the dal overnite and pressure cook the lentil next day or you can even use aslow cooker, but dont forget to saok dal overnite.
Black gram lentil cooked over  low heat for couple of hours added to the rich creamy flavor of this dish, making it a comforting and special treat. You can enjoy these warm lentils with rice or Tandoori naan.



Dal Makhani

Ingredients


2 cups black gram lentils
1/2  cup red kidney bean (Rajma)
5 cups water ( to soak the lentil's)
1 small onion chopped finely
2 to 3 fresh cloves of garlic
1 inch ginger
1/2 tsp cumin seeds
2 tsp salt
1 tsp red chili powder
3 to 4 green chilies
1 medium tomatoes chopped fine
1 tsp freshly ground garam masala powder(dry roast in a skillet, on low heat for about 5 minutes,cool and dry grind to a powder :- 1 tsp coriander seeds, 2 small cardamom, 2 to 3 cloves,1 stick cinnamon, 2 to 3 peppercorns)
1/3 cup fresh cream or take same amount milk for lighter version
2 tsp oil


Method


1. Wash well the lentils, and Soak both lentils overnight.


2. Next day pressure cook the lentils ,adding chopped onions, cumin seeds, chopped ginger, garlic,salt and red cili powder and about 4 cups water. Allow to cook for about an hour till the lentils are soft and light mix the cooked lentils with a spoon and keep aside.


3. In a pan, heat 2 tsp oil, add chopped tomatoes, allow to sizzle, add garam masala powder, chopped green chilies, add 1 tsp salt and 1/2 tsp red chili powder, stir in the cooked lentils and continue cooking lentils on low heat by adding 1/2 cup water. 

4. Cook for about 20 to 30 minutes. Add fresh cream and serve warm with rice or Indian bread.

title: Vegetarian Biryani
excerpt: Vegetarian Biryani is a  favorite in my family. When I got married, I didn't have much experience in cooking, so I decided to learn few dishes and this is …
html:
Vegetarian Biryani is a  favorite in my family. When I got married, I didn't have much experience in cooking, so I decided to learn few dishes and this is an outcome of that learning.
Biryani  is prepared by cooking rice and layering it with vegetables and spices.  Saffron and mint leaves are used in this dish that give it a flavorful aroma. Its a great dish for entertaining or as a main dish too.

Ingredients
2 cups Basmati rice
2 cups water to cook the rice
1 medium carrot chopped in cubes
1/2 cup peas (semi cooked or fresh)
1/4 cup cut cauliflower florets
1/4 cup  fresh green beans chopped in  small cubes
2  medium size onion pureed
1 medium size onion sliced thin and shallow fry to use later.
2  medium tomato pureed
2 tsp ginger garlic paste
4 to 5 green chilies chopped
3 to 4 mint leaves
2 tsp salt
1 tsp red chili powder
1/2 tsp turmeric
2 to 3 bay leaves
2 to 3 small cardamom, peel and use the seeds
1 tsp Freshly ground garam masala powder/ready masala powder  available in Indian stores.
5 tbsp oil
4 to 5  strands of saffron, soak saffron strands  in 1/4 cup milk.
1/4 cashews ,shallow fried.
1/4 cup water

Method:
1. Rinse the rice well ,soak in 2 cups water for about 10 to 15 minute ,cook rice in open pan for approximately 20 minutes, till fluffy and cooked, but don't overcook the rice,drain and keep aside. 
2. Heat oil in a skillet,add  onions, bay leaves saute till  onions appear golden brown,add in the spices,ginger garlic paste,green chilies, small cardamom and tomato puree. Cook another few minutes,add in the vegetables, garam masala and 1/4 cup water, cover with a lid  to cook the vegetables over medium heat for about 10 minutes. Keep the ready vegetable gravy aside.
3. To start layering, dish out a layer of cooked rice on the bottom of  a rectangular baking  dish.Add few sprinkles of saffron milk over the layered rice,next add a big tbsp of cooked vegetable gravy. Follow with the cooked rice layer, Layer with fried onions,cashew and chopped mint leaves. Again follow with rice layer,followed with vegetable gravy layer.
4. Repeat these layers, Cover with silver foil and bake in oven for about 15 to 20 minutes.Take out of oven, garnish with finely chopped coriander leaves Serve hot biryani  with raita or  plain yogurt.

Rajma a popular dish  in all North Indian homes,but now it is also enjoyed by everyone. At my place we like to  eat this dish with plain rice, and usually prepare it on a Lazy Sunday afternoon .
Rajma is prepared by using Red  kidney bean, it is full of protein and good for health. The tip to cooking Rajma is to plan ahead and soak the beans overnight and cook it the next day.





Rajma



Ingredients:
200gm red kidney beans
2 cups water for soaking beans overnight
1 medium sized onion chopped fine
1 tsp ginger garlic paste
2 to 3 green chili chopped fine
2 tsp salt
1 tsp red chili powder
1/2 tsp turmeric
4 tbsp oil

1 medium size tomato grated
Method:
1. Wash thoroughly and soak overnight the red kidney beans,next day pressure cook the beans using  2cups water ,add  1 tsp salt,red chili powder and allow the beans to  pressure cook for  30 to 40 minutes or  till they are soft and cooked. Keep aside.
2. Heat oil in a pan,add ginger garlic paste,add onions, stir till onions appear golden in color,add in green chilies,turmeric and tomatoes.Continue to cook another 5 to 10 minutes, add in  boiled kidney beans(along with the water) continue to  cook another 10  minutes, check for salt ,add 1 tsp, if less salt.Add freshly prepared garam masala powder,boil another 5 minutes ,till the gravy appears thick.Serve hot with steamed rice or Indian bread.

Valentine Cupcakes

title: Kutch Speciality - Dabeli.
excerpt: Friends, today I am going to share with you a speciality dish from Kutch. It is called Dabeli. People in Western part of India are familiar with this dish as it is …
html:
Friends, today I am going to share with you a speciality dish from Kutch. It is called Dabeli. People in Western part of India are familiar with this dish as it is available in Gujarat and major cities of Maharashtra. Others may not be aware of it. However, once you try it,  you will enjoy it and will want to have it again. I learnt this dish from my mother in law. She was born and did her schooling in Mandvi, a small town in Kutch. Before I start writing about the dish, I would like to start with saying few things about Kutch. 


Kutch district is a district of Gujarat state in western India. Covering an area of 45,652 km², it is the largest district of India.  Kutch District is surrounded by the Gulf of Kutch and the Arabian Sea in south and west, while northern and eastern parts are surrounded by the Rann of Kutch. To the North of Kutch is the Pakistan border. The Rann of Kutch boasts of beautiful white sand. The language spoken predominantly  is Kutchi language, sort of a mix of Gujarati, Sindhi, and Hindi. The place is becoming a popular tourist attraction after Gujarat Government started promoting the natural beauty of the place. Credit also needs to go to the popular ad campaign featuring none other than the Big B - Mr. Amitabh Bachchan. The Rann Utsav, in December, and Kite festival in the month of January have added to the popularity of this place. These festivals are attended by thousands of people from across the world.  Here are couple of photos of Rann of Kutch.

Rann of Kutch

title: A little bit of Italy in my Cuisine.
excerpt: The other day we wanted to try out something different for Diner. In my family we love Italian cuisine. And for the very first time I decided to try to make Chicken …
html:
The other day we wanted to try out something different for Diner. In my family we love Italian cuisine. And for the very first time I decided to try to make Chicken Marsala, as we all love that dish. The dish is prepared by using boneless chicken breast and cooking them in the Marsala wine , which originates from a coastal town in Italy,by the name Marsala. It is an elegant dish and initially I was definitely hesitant a bit as I have never tried cooking with wine. But now I'm glad I tried it out, and it came out just nice, my family loved the taste , so it's worth the try and do share your experience cooking it too:) Happy cooking!!!



Chicken Marsala






Ingredients:
4-5   boneless chicken breasts
1/2 cup flour for coating
1/2 cup  sliced mushrooms
2 tbsp butter
1/2 cup Marsala wine
1 cup chicken stock
2  tbsp olive oil
2 tsp salt
1 tsp onion powder, 1tsp cayenne pepper,1 tsp garlic powder,1 tsp dried oregano,1 tsp dried thyme.
2 tsp freshly ground black pepper.


1. In a shallow dish combine flour,salt, black pepper,garlic powder,onion powder, cayenne pepper, dried  oregano,dried thyme.
2. Using a meat tenderizer pound (flatten) the  chicken breast to 1/4 inch thin and coat with the seasoned  flour mixture , shaking off any excess.
3.Heat a skillet,add olive oil ,  butter and cook the chicken breasts to a golden brown color on both side for 3 to 4 minutes.Remove and keep on a plate. In the same skillet cook the mushrooms till they sweat and water evaporates,add the Marsala wine,making sure the flame is on low heat. Bring to a boil,scrapping the browned tidbits from the pan,add in stock,allow the sauce to thicken and transfer the chicken breast back  to the pan and cook for another 5 to 10 minutes.
 To give the dish a creamier taste, you could add in 1/4 cup milk or heavy cream in the end.
You could also add boiled vegetables,garlic toast or a salad as they all go great with this dish.

Ingredients
2 pounds chicken (cleaned and cut into medium size pieces)
3 tbsp ginger garlic paste
2 medium size onions chopped
4 tbsp oil
Ingredients (For Marinating)
2 tsp red chili powder
salt to taste
4 tsp coriander powder
1 tsp turmeric powder
Ingredients(For Dry Masala)
4 tbsp whole coriander seeds
2 tbsp uncooked rice
1 tbsp fennel seeds
1 tbsp whole peppercorns
2 tsp cumin seeds
8 to 10 whole red dried chilies
Ingredients (for garnish)
1 green bell pepper sliced
10 to 12 curry leaves
1 tsp fresh coriander leaves chopped
2 tsp oil

Method:
1.Take red chili powder,turmeric,coriander powder ,salt and rub this marinade onto the chicken pieces and keep chicken marinated for an hour or two.
2. Heat a pan, and on medium heat  dry roast the masala ingredients and grind to a fine powder.
3. Heat 4 tbsp oil in a thick bottomed pan, add in onions, brown to a golden color, add ginger garlic paste and marinated chicken pieces. Stir  for  15 to 20 minutes. Add 1cup (200ml) water,continue to cook over medium heat.
4. Add  powdered masala to  chicken  continue cooking another 10 to 15 minutes until the chicken is cooked.
5. Heat 2 tsp oil shallow fry bell pepper and curry leaves, remove and  garnish over the cooked chicken, sprinkle some fresh chopped coriander.

title: Carrot Pudding (Gajjar Halwa) Recipe
excerpt: Halwa is a sweet and delicious dessert of India. It is prepared in many different ways. Carrot Pudding is a popular Indian desert and it is prepared by using carrots and …
html:
Halwa is a sweet and delicious dessert of India. It is prepared in many different ways. Carrot Pudding is a popular Indian desert and it is prepared by using carrots and milk.


Growing up in India , I remember the times when my mom made this dessert and the sweet aroma from the cooked dessert filled the kitchen and other rooms. I have tried to create the same taste, so wanted to share the recipe. It is really easy and the result is rewarding ....hot halwa in cold season..makes a good combination.


Ingredients:
2 pound peeled and grated carrots.
1 cup milk
1/2 cup / 200 gm condensed milk
2 to 3 tbsp sugar
3 tbsp clarified butter( ghee)
3 to 4 small cardamom powdered
50 gm cashews and raisins for garnish
1/4 cup almonds powdered
2 to 3 strands of saffron


Method:
1. Heat 1 tsp ghee in a kadai (wok). Add cashews, raisins saute for few seconds, remove and keep aside for garnish.
2. In the same wok, add 3 tbsp clarified butter, add in the grated carrots, stir for about 5 minutes.
3. Pour in the milk, further cook till the milk evaporates.Now add the condensed milk and sugar.Keep stirring well till the milk gets absorbed. Add almonds, cardamom powder & 2 to 3 strands of saffron.
4. Allow to cook for another about 10 minutes on high to medium heat, stirring  till all the liquid evaporates, and halwa turns nice deeper color. Garnish with nuts and serve hot.


You can also top it with cream and berries.

wet and work as a sauce or marinade.

They come in all varieties and differ from State to State. For example, in Maharashtra (that is the western part of India) where peanuts are common, the chutney prepared uses peanuts and garlic. The chutney is called Thetcha - it has green chilies too and that gives it a fiercy(sharp and spicy)taste.  In Kashmir (Northern part of the country) we have chutney prepared using apples and walnut.

In the Southern part we have coconut chutney that is popular. 

In Gujarat, it is the chundda (sweet mango chutney) prepared with sour mangoes,  spices , jaggery and sugar

Today let's prepare green chutney using fresh coriander leaves, ginger, garlic, lemon juice along with salt.

title: Chicken Shawarma
excerpt: Shawarma is a savory, and very aromatic Middle Eastern dish, that is prepared by cooking chicken pieces, preferably thigh meat with spices and sauces and rolled …
html:
Shawarma is a savory, and very aromatic Middle Eastern dish, that is prepared by cooking chicken pieces, preferably thigh meat with spices and sauces and rolled into a roll that has meat, slices of pickled onions, spices. It is enjoyed as a hearty snack or even at night time as a meal. Chicken is marinated for hours and usually cooked rotisserie style, and then the cooked chicken is made a little crisp, not burnt and thinly sliced or shaved. Filled into pita pockets, along with thinly sliced salad, onions, olives and for that extra zest add some pickles and tahini sauce.

But to make it at home, you don't need a rotisserie or spit cooking. All that is required is a baking sheet and oven to cook the chicken. ( preferably thigh meat instead of breast meat of chicken)


Ingredients 

1 pound cut thigh meat ( boneless and skinless)

For chicken marination:

1/2 tsp cumin powder

1/2 tsp coriander powder

Salt to taste

1/2 tsp cayenne pepper

1/2 lemon juice

1/4 tsp cloves powder

1 tsp freshly grated garlic

2 tsp olive oil

1 tsp tomato paste 

1 tsp black pepper powdered


For the sauce to go with shawarma

1 lemon juice

Salt to taste

4 tsp Tahini paste (Tahini is made from sesame seeds )

1/4 tsp cumin powder

1/4 cup water 


1 packet ready Pita pockets bread 

1/2 cup fresh green salad leaves 

1/4 cup olives



Method: To cook chicken

1. First, clean and marinate the chicken thigh in a medium bowl, using the ingredients mentioned.Cover and leave for at least 2 to 3 hours.

Next, heat oven to 375 degrees. Using a baking sheet that is sprayed with little oil, place the  marinated chicken pieces onto a baking sheet.

2.Brush the pieces with some little olive oil, and continue baking for about 20 minutes, till the chicken is cooked.

3.You can put the oven setting to broil, just for a 2 to 3 minutes, to crisp the edges of the chicken, but at this time be extra observant as chicken can burn. 

Remove and keep aside.

To prepare the Tahini sauce:

1. In a little bowl, take tahini sauce, add in lemon juice and mix both well, adding little water to 

make it a creamy, yet honey like consistency. 

2.Season with salt and cumin powder. Cover and store in a jar, for use as a dipping or sauce for Shawarma. 

Filling:

1. Warm a pita bread. Open it like a pocket and the cooked chicken, add some salad leaves and then drizzle some tahini sauce.

You can also prepare the chicken on a heavy skillet, over there gas stove, if you don't have the oven.

Enjoy!

title: Bombay Dabeli pav
excerpt: Dabeli is a very popular street food in Kutch Gujarat, India. It has now gained popularity worldwide as a quick and easy snack. It is prepared by adding spicy …
html:
Dabeli is a very popular street food in Kutch Gujarat, India. It has now gained popularity worldwide as a quick and easy snack. It is prepared by adding spicy potatoes to a pav (bun) with some garlic chutney, tamarind chutney. Garnish with sev and pomegranate seeds and masala peanuts. This mix of tangy and sweet give it the perfect taste you won't forget.

There is place in Gujarat called Kutch where this dish originated. 

Ingredients:

6 to 8 medium size potatoes (pressure cook them)

2 tsp Dabeli masala powder (available in Indian stores or online)

Oil for preparing 

1/2 cup ready tamarind chutney (available in indian store)

200 gms  Dabeli peanuts (Jabsons peanuts are available in Indian grocery) or you use plain roasted peanuts, and add little dabeli masala to it.

1 dozen buns or pav (available in stores)


For garlic chutney (You can also use ready store bought garlic chutney or make it) 

1/2 cup peeled fresh garlic 

2 tsp salt

2 tsp coriander powder

1 tsp cumin seeds 

2 tsp red chili powder

1 tsp fresh lemon juice

1/4 cup water


Method

1.Using a blender grind all the above items for garlic chutney. Keep aside. Omit this step if using store bought garlic chutney.

2. Pressure cook potatoes, take 2 cups of water, add potatoes, and cook for 2 to 3 whistles,  cool and peel the skin and mash them. Keep aside.

3. In a medium sized kadai, heat 2 to 3 tbsp vegetable oil, add in 2 tsp red chili powder, 2 tsp dabeli powder, 1/4 cup prepared garlic chutney, add in 1/4 cup of emlee chutney. Emlee chutney, is sweet and tangy so it gives a good balance. Stir in the mashed potatoes, add dabeli powder, add salt. Check for salt, dabeli masala, if needed add more. Squeeze 1/2 a fresh lemon juice.

4. In a small pan, add 2 tsp oil, add in the peanuts, add 1 tsp red chili powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, 1 tsp chaat powder. 

5. Enjoy prepared dabeli by scooping a spoonful on the bun or pav, add some peanuts and some garlic chutney if needed.

title: Bombay Pav bhaji
excerpt: Pav bhaji is a vegetarian dish, that originated in Mumbai (aka, Bombay) where it is eaten as a popular street food. The dish originated in Maharashtra as a fast …
html:
Pav bhaji is a vegetarian dish, that originated in Mumbai (aka, Bombay) where it is eaten as a popular street food. The dish originated in Maharashtra as a fast lunch time dish for mill workers back in 1850's.

Later, as we all know its popularity grew further to become one of the most beloved Indian street food.

One can make it more healthy by adding more vegetables and helping parents that feel their child misses on eating some veggies.  You can alter the spice level so that children can enjoy the health benefits of eating pav bhaji. The bhaji (vegetable) is prepared by pressure cooking the veggies and making a thick puree ( mashing them) and adding them to cooked onions and tomatoes mixture. It is enjoyed with buttered pav (or bun)


Ingredients:

1 pound or 4 to 5 medium size potatoes washed and peel

1 medium sized onion, chopped finely

1 medium size tomato, chopped finely

1/4 ready tomato puree ( or using 2 small tomatoes, and a blender, add 1/4 cup water and blend to smooth puree)

200 gms frozen ready chopped carrots and peas 

1/2 cup clean and chopped cauliflower

1 small chinese brinjal chopped roughly

1/2 capsicum finely chopped

2 tsp pav bhaji powder ( I like to use store bought brands like Everest or Badshah)

1/2 lemon juice

1 tsp red chili powder

Salt to taste

1 tsp garam masala powder (available in indian store)

50 gms butter (your choice)

2 to 3 tsp vegetable oil

In a pressure cooker, add 2 cups water, peeled potatoes cut into cubes, 1 cup green frozen peas and carrots.

1.Heat a kadai, add in oil and butter. Add in finely chopped onions, allow them to get little translucent, add in green chilies, add finely chopped capsicum, ginger garlic paste, tomatoes. Stir for few minutes, add in salt, red chili powder, pav bhaji powder, lemon juice and keep stirring on medium heat. Add in 1/4 cup tomato puree. As the mixture comes together, add in 1/4 cup water and continue stirring.

2. Next, add the mashed vegetables and potatoes mixture and mix well. Check for salt and pav bhaji masala, add some, if needed. 

3. Garnish with finely chopped fresh coriander and butter pav or bun.

4. Use a flat pan or skillet, add 2 tsp butter, allow it to sizzle. Cut the pav into two and place it on the hot pan to butter it. Enjoy with bhaji ( spiced vegetables and freshly chopped onions and lemon)

title: Bombay Masala Omelette
excerpt: Eggs are so versatile, and my family loves eating eggs. We also find them as a good source of protein, while easy to prepare and quick too. Here I am sharing the …
html:
Eggs are so versatile, and my family loves eating eggs. We also find them as a good source of protein, while easy to prepare and quick too.

Here I am sharing the recipe of masala omelette. The word masala refers to adding some spices to the otherwise plain egg. We love our sunday morning with eggs and toast.


Ingredients

2 eggs (brown or white)

1/4 onion chopped finely 

2 thai chilies (optional) finely chopped 

1/2 tsp red chili powder

Salt to taste

Vegetable oil or butter

1/4 cup finely chopped fresh coriander

1/4 tsp turmeric powder

1/4 tsp cumin seeds

1. Using a medium bowl, whisk 2 eggs, add in salt, red chili powder, turmeric. Keep aside.

2.Heat a flat skillet, add in cumin seeds, allow them to splutter a little. Add in finely chopped onions, add green chilies and fresh coriander. Next, add in finely chopped tomatoes. Saute for a minute on medium heat.

3. Now add in the egg mixture, and allow it to spread till the sides of the skillet, cook it for 2 to 3 minutes, before  carefully flipping it, to cook on both sides. Next, fold it and place prepared omelette onto a serving plate along with two toasts and some ketchup. Enjoy.

If you're preparing more omelettes, just repeat the above steps with another two eggs.

title: Bombay Frankee
excerpt: Bombay Frankee is a popular Mumbai street food. This dish consists of a tortilla shaped flat roti, that is cooked on a flat griddle and filled with spicy vegetable …
html:
Bombay Frankee is a popular Mumbai street food. This dish consists of a tortilla shaped flat roti, that is cooked on a flat griddle and filled with spicy vegetable potatoes, more like a tikki or use paneer tandoori tikkas, also some cooked stir fried vegetables and  with freshly chopped onions, chaat powder and green chilies to give the spicy tangy flavor.

 If your cooking a non veg frankee, heat the indian flat bread (roti) on the griddle, add a spoonful of beaten egg, flip and allow the egg wash to coat one side of the roti. Next, add  cooked chicken, along with finely chopped onions, that are dipped in vinegar, along with raw mango powder (amchur) to give it a tangy spicy flavor. Similarly, you can also prepare Mutton frankee, by replacing cooked chicken and adding cooked mutton curry.



Ingredient:

Chicken frankee

1 pound chicken thigh meat, cut into small one inch cubes

2 tsp freshly grated or bottled ginger garlic paste

1 tsp finely chopped green chilies 

1 tsp garam masala 

1 medium onion chopped finely

1 medium tomato chopped finely

Salt to taste

2 tsp ketchup

1/4 tsp turmeric

1 tsp red chilli powder

1 tsp coriander powder


For Filling 

1/4 cup amchur powder

1/4 cup fine chopped onions in 1/4 cup plain vinegar

1 egg beaten and add 1/4 tsp salt to it , for egg wash 

Assemble:

Heat oil in a kadai, add cumin seeds, small cardamom, cloves, and saute the onions on medium heat.

As they become translucent add in the chicken, cook till they appear cooked. Add in turmeric, red chilli powder, salt, coriander powder and a dash of ketchup. Add in tomatoes and stir till oil separates. 

Next, add in 1/2 cup water and cover to cook. Half way through check the chicken and add salt, if needed.

Close burner and keep aside.

For assembling:

Heat flat roti on a warm griddle, coat one side with egg wash. Next, flip and cook the egg side for 2 minutes. Take out on plate, add a teaspoon of the finely chopped onions, add 2 tsp of cooked chicken, sprinkle pinch of amchur powder, add green chilies. Now roll the indian flat bread and enjoy it like a wrap.


This versatile Indian street food is sure to win your taste.

1 Egg
Salt to taste

1/2 lemon juice

For home made potato fries:
4 to 5 Russet potatoes
Vegetable oil to fry
Salt to taste
ketchup 


 Method:

2.  First, season the cod fish fillets by sprinkling salt and black pepper on each fillet. Drizzle a little Worcestershire sauce, and marinate for about 10 minutes. Now add flour in a plate, beat the egg in a bowl, season with salt. Lastly, put panko or rice flour ready in a plate.

Mutton Rogan josh, a favorite dish, liked by my sister. We used to  order it every time we went out with our parents.

A very aromatic dish and the origin of this dish is from Kashmir (Northern part of India)


                                        Mutton Rogan josh
Ingredients
2 pounds mutton (tender goat meat, preferably leg or shoulder with bone
2 to 3 whole cardamoms
2 bay leaves
1/2 tsp asafetida (hing)
4  garlic cloves 
3 to 4 small green cardamom 
1 small stick cinnamon
Salt as per taste
 1 tsp sugar
1 tsp ginger powder
1 tsp fennel powder
2 tsp red chilly powder (kashmiri powder)
1/4 cup plain yogurt
1/4 cup oil for cooking or ghee (your choice)



Roghan Josh 
Method:
1.Clean and pat dry mutton pieces. In a medium sized bowl, add yogurt and mutton. To this add in 1 tsp salt and leave to marinate for about 30 minutes.
2. Heat ghee (clarified butter) or oil, in a pressure cook utensil. Add whole cardamoms, bay leaves, cinnamon stick, cloves, small cardamoms. Add asafetida powder. As the spices begin to sizzle, add in marinated mutton, continue stirring ,cooking on low to medium heat for about 20 minutes. As the mutton appears to brown, lower the heat.
3.Take 2 tsp red chilly powder (Kashmir) add it to 1/4 cup of room temperature water, stir and add this to the mutton. This will give the mutton the reddish color.
4. Add ginger powder and fennel powder. Add salt,  sugar and stir to cook for another 10 minutes. Add 1/2 cup water and pressure cook, for 20 minutes or another 10 more minutes, till mutton appears well done and soft.
 Garnish with a sprig of mint leaves, serve hot with Basmati rice or enjoy with a Tandoori Naan , your choice:)
Pls note: You can use lamb meat too instead of mutton.

                                         Yakhani Pulav
Yakhani Pulav is a rice dish, cooked with meat. Instead of using water to cook rice, we use mutton or chicken stock.
Whenever, we went to my Aunt's place, she used to cook this for us, and this became one of my favorite rice dish. It is wholesome and very comfortingly nutritious.
Yakhani Pulav
Ingredients 
2 cups  Basmati Rice
1 pound of mutton chops  
2 medium size onions sliced thinly
1 cup tomato pureed
2 tsp freshly grated ginger 
2 tsp freshly grated garlic
1 tsp finely chopped green chilies
1 tsp Shahi jeera
Salt as per taste
2 cups water
1/4 cup Vegetable oil
2 medium sized roma tomatoes, pureed
 4 to 5  black pepper cons
2 black cardamon
1 inch cinnamon stick
2 bay leaves
1 tsp garam masala 
Finely chopped mint leaves
Method:
1. Heat 2 tbsp ghee in a medium size pan, add black cardamom, cloves, cinnamon, sliced onions and saute till the onions appear golden in color.  Add in the mutton chops, while stirring another 5 to 10 minutes. 
Add 1 cup water and cover with a lid, cooking for another 10 minutes and then strain all the liquid. this is the stock you use later.
Keep the mutton chops aside. 
2. Heat a tsp of vegetable oil. Add Shahi jeera, ginger garlic and pureed tomatoes. To this add the mutton chops, saute for about 2 to 3 minutes. Add salt, garam masala, now add in the rice.
3. Stir together and add in the stock and 1 more cup of water. Cook covered with a lid, on low to medium heat for another 10 to 15 minutes, till water is evaporated and rice are cooked.
Garnish with finely chopped mint leaves and serve with yogurt or just as is :) Enjoy
